headline: Last session: Sensex dropped 571 points as Indian benchmark indices logged their eighth consecutive weekly decline

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 5 October.

why: Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) offloaded over Rs 35,000 crore worth of Indian equities in September.
Sharp losses in sector-specific indices, with Nifty Auto slipping 3% in the last session.
Sustained selling pressure leading to an eight-week losing streak, the longest in 25 years.
Significant market capital erosion wiping out around Rs 6 lakh crore in market capitalization.
whatHappening: Sensex dropped 570.59 points while Nifty closed at 22,421.95 on the last trading session.
29 companies are scheduled to list this week with grey market premiums signaling potential gains of up to 59%.
Deepwater gas price ceiling was increased to $9.89 per MMBtu with APM cap set at $7.
IT sector Q2 earnings preview suggests muted growth with steady margins and focus on AI deflation.
summary:
On the last trading session, Indian benchmark indices extended their losing streak to eight consecutive weeks, with Sensex dropping 571 points.
Persistent FPI selling saw over Rs 35,000 crore withdrawn in September, eroding trillions in market capitalization.
Markets are closed today for the weekend and will reopen on Monday, October 5, alongside a heavy lineup of 29 IPO listings.
